{"rule": "Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.", "text": "The path along the water was paved in places and not in others, and Tomas could not tell whether the paving had once been continuous and had failed, or had never been finished. The boy walked on the outside, nearest the river, and Tomas found he had shifted to put himself there instead without deciding to.

"You did that before," the boy said.

"Did what?"

"Moved me." He did not sound troubled by it. He sounded as though he were keeping a list.

They passed a bench with a plaque on it. Tomas slowed to read the name and found he could read every letter and still could not hold the name in his head long enough to know it. The boy waited. He was good at waiting; it seemed to cost him nothing.

"Do you remember the house?" Tomas asked.

The boy considered this the way he considered everything, thoroughly and without evident effort. "There was a window that wasn't there," he said. "And the stairs went up more than they went down."

"Yes."

"You remember it too."

"I remember being in it." That was different, and they both seemed to know it was different, and neither of them said so.

Ahead, the river bent, and the far bank drew closer, and the walkers there had thinned to one, a woman in a grey coat who had stopped and was looking, for the first time, directly across.

The boy's hand tightened. Tomas did not know which of them had done it.

"Keep going," the boy said, and they did."}
